mito src.cel
cmp stdout want.txt

-- src.cel --
// Examples derived from the CEL two variable comprehension docs with changes
// required to conform to JSON-serialised testing here.
[
	[1, 2, 3].transformList(i, v, (i * v) + v),
	[1, 2, 3].transformList(i, v, i % 2 == 0, (i * v) + v),
	// Map iteration order is non-deterministic, so do explicit checks for the
	// following two tests.
	{'greeting': 'hello', 'farewell': 'goodbye'}.transformList(k, _, k).as(res,
		res.size() == 2 &&
		res.exists(e, e == 'greeting') &&
		res.exists(e, e == 'farewell')
	),
	{'greeting': 'hello', 'farewell': 'goodbye'}.transformList(_, v, v).as(res,
		res.size() == 2 &&
		res.exists(e, e == 'hello') &&
		res.exists(e, e == 'goodbye')
	),

	// The first two examples here deviate from the CEL documentation since
	// we depend on serialisation to JSON which cannot have integer keys,
	// so we have a second transformMapEntry to stringify the key.
	[1, 2, 3].transformMap(i, v, (i * v) + v).transformMapEntry(k, v, {string(k): v}),
	[1, 2, 3].transformMap(i, v, i % 2 == 0, (i * v) + v).transformMapEntry(k, v, {string(k): v}),
	{'greeting': 'hello'}.transformMap(k, v, v + '!'),

	{'greeting': 'hello'}.transformMapEntry(k, v, {v: k}),
	[1, 2, 3].transformMapEntry(i, v, {string(v): i}),
	try({'greeting': 'aloha', 'farewell': 'aloha'}.transformMapEntry(k, v, {v: k})),
]
